analysis.evidence: וַתְּהִי links the subject רֵאשִׁית מַמְלַכְתּוֹ (“the beginning of his kingdom”) to the four cities that constituted that beginning. The feminine singular verb agrees with the head noun רֵאשִׁית.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וַ is prefixed to a Qal wayyiqtol, third-person feminine singular, agreeing with רֵאשִׁית.
analysis.sense: to be in a state or condition

analysis.evidence: רֵאשִׁית מַמְלַכְתּוֹ means “the beginning of his kingdom.” The four cities that follow identify where his kingdom began.
analysis.morphology: Feminine singular common noun in the construct state, followed by מַמְלַכְתּוֹ (“his kingdom”).

analysis.evidence: The verse names Babel, Erech, Accad, and Calneh in the land of Shinar as the beginning of his kingdom. The list of cities identifies the kingdom as the territory he ruled.
analysis.morphology: Feminine singular common noun in the construct state with a third-person masculine singular possessive suffix.

draft.change: Add בָּבֶל as a place-name article under nouns/, keyed to its own consonants בבל.
draft.definition: Babel (Babylon), a city in the land of Shinar.
draft.evidence: Genesis 10:10 lists Babel first among the places that formed the beginning of Nimrod’s kingdom. Genesis 11:8–9 identifies Babel as the name of the city.

analysis.evidence: After רֵאשִׁית מַמְלַכְתּוֹ, “the beginning of his kingdom,” בָּבֶל opens a list with Erech, Akkad, and Calneh. The closing phrase בְּאֶרֶץ שִׁנְעָר locates them in the land of Shinar.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun. The initial בּ belongs to the place name. The word has no prefix or suffix.

draft.change: Append the Hebrew place name אֶרֶךְ to 2rk under its consonantal filing key ארכ. Revise the editorial note to retain the identification with Uruk and distinguish the name’s origin from the Hebrew verb אָרַךְ.
draft.definition: Erech, a city in the land of Shinar named among the first centers of Nimrod’s kingdom.
draft.evidence: In Gen.10.10 the repeated conjunction links Erech with Babel, Akkad and Calneh, and בְּאֶרֶץ שִׁנְעָר locates the four places.

analysis.evidence: Genesis 10:10 places אֶרֶךְ between Babel and Akkad in the list of places that formed the beginning of Nimrod’s kingdom. The closing phrase בְּאֶרֶץ שִׁנְעָר locates them in the land of Shinar.
analysis.morphology: The prefixed conjunction וְ joins the proper noun אֶרֶךְ to the preceding city name בָּבֶל.

draft.change: Add a Hebrew place-name entry for אַכַּד under nouns/ with the sense city-of-akkad.
draft.definition: Akkad, a city in Shinar that formed part of Nimrod’s early kingdom.
draft.evidence: Genesis 10:10 names Akkad alongside Babel, Erech and Calneh in the land of Shinar.

analysis.evidence: Genesis 10:10 places אַכַּד between Erech and Calneh in the list of places that formed the beginning of Nimrod’s kingdom. The closing phrase בְּאֶרֶץ שִׁנְעָר locates them in the land of Shinar.
analysis.morphology: The prefixed conjunction וְ means “and” and joins the proper noun אַכַּד to the preceding place name.
analysis.sense: The city of Akkad in the land of Shinar.

draft.change: Add a place-name article under nouns/ using the name’s own consonants, כלנה, as its key. The occurrence provides no evidence for a derivation from כלמ.
draft.definition: Calneh, a city in Shinar included in the beginning of Nimrod’s kingdom.
draft.evidence: Genesis 10:10 coordinates וְכַלְנֵה with the preceding city names and closes the list with “in the land of Shinar.”

analysis.evidence: Calneh follows Babel, Erech and Akkad as the fourth place named at the beginning of Nimrod’s kingdom. The phrase בְּאֶרֶץ שִׁנְעָר locates the places in Shinar.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וְ, “and,” prefixes the proper noun כַּלְנֵה. The initial כ loses its dagesh after the conjunction.

analysis.evidence: בְּאֶרֶץ שִׁנְעָר locates the four named cities in the land of Shinar. אֶרֶץ denotes the territory identified by שִׁנְעָר.
analysis.morphology: The preposition בְּ means “in.” The noun אֶרֶץ is of common gender and stands in the singular construct before שִׁנְעָר.

draft.change: Add a place-name entry for Shinar under its own consonants. The source gloss “ewe” and proposed root שנס lack support here.
draft.definition: Shinar is the land in which Genesis 10:10 locates Babel, Erech, Accad, and Calneh.
draft.evidence: The phrase בְּאֶרֶץ שִׁנְעָר identifies the region containing the four cities.

analysis.evidence: After listing the four cities where Nimrod’s kingdom began, Genesis 10:10 locates them together בְּאֶרֶץ שִׁנְעָר. The word שִׁנְעָר names their land.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun with no prefix or suffix. It completes the construct phrase בְּאֶרֶץ שִׁנְעָר, “in the land of Shinar.”
analysis.sense: The land containing Babel, Erech, Accad, and Calneh.
